title: POST /podcasts can resurrect a deleted non-podcast feed

evidence.quote:
select(MediaFeed).where(MediaFeed.url == feed_data.url)
...
existing.deleted_at = None
...
return existing

reasoning: The route validates that the request body says feed_type='podcast', but the shared create helper looks up any existing feed by URL without constraining feed_type. If that row is soft-deleted, the helper reactivates it and updates several fields, but it never updates or checks existing.feed_type. A POST /podcasts request using the URL of a soft-deleted YouTube feed can therefore return 201 with a MediaFeed whose feed_type is still 'youtube'. That violates the route contract and leaves the newly returned feed absent from podcast list/update/delete flows that filter by feed_type='podcast'.
reproduction: Seed a soft-deleted MediaFeed with feed_type='youtube' and url='https://example.com/feed.xml', then POST /podcasts with feed_type='podcast' and the same url. The helper returns the reactivated row without changing feed_type, so the response is a YouTube feed from the podcast endpoint.
recommendation: In _create_media_feed, include MediaFeed.feed_type == feed_data.feed_type in the duplicate lookup, or explicitly reject a same-URL soft-deleted row whose feed_type differs from feed_data.feed_type. If cross-type URL reuse is intentionally disallowed, return 409 instead of reactivating the wrong type.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and a repo search found no direct create_podcast_feed or POST /podcasts route tests covering cross-type soft-delete reactivation.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI route test that creates or seeds a soft-deleted youtube MediaFeed, posts the same URL to /podcasts with feed_type='podcast', and asserts the endpoint either returns 409 or returns a feed whose feed_type is 'podcast' and is visible in GET /podcasts.
minimumFixScope: Update _create_media_feed duplicate/reactivation logic and add route-level regression coverage for soft-deleted same-URL feeds with a different feed_type.
